correctness.rationale: Under 3<=r<s, t>=2, Hanely et al. Proposition 4.4 is the exact full-dimensional H-description on the rank hyperplane. Orthogonal projection gives coordinate normal length sqrt((n-1)/n) and tail normal length sqrt(st/n). Every center yields three aggregate upper bounds on the rescaled inradius; a two-block constant center exists whenever the corresponding four interval comparisons hold, with the fourth strictly redundant. Equality forces precisely the claimed point, cube-section, or simplex center loci; ties are unique. All stated facets are genuine via explicit relative-interior points. A standalone fresh-code replay solved 495 unsymmetrized Chebyshev linear programs, verified primal feasibility, tested source facets by independent vertex ranks, and checked both tie examples. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace proof.

value.rationale: Panhandle matroids are the natural hypersimplex pieces used in paving-matroid constructions. The exact intrinsic inball describes how this canonical Euclidean metric changes under their single correlated truncation. The theorem is an all-parameter classification identifying three distinct sharp, nonempty phases and high-dimensional versus unique center sets; in the strict phases the centers are a point, a cube section, and a simplex, respectively, and the two nonunique dimensions can grow without bound. These are motivated structural facts, not arbitrary parameter sampling or a minor numerical gain.
